A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 32-page paper, Moral Alignment for LLM Agents, including the complete appendix. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content on pages 2–32; page 1 differs only in its arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on moral fine-tuning, unlearning selfish strategies, and generalization across matrix games, with further robustness and qualitative analyses in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experimental results in Sections 4–5 and the appendix, including learning curves, moral-regret comparisons, and model-response examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Table 1 retain the same Gemma2-2b-it model, PPO fine-tuning procedure, intrinsic reward functions, illegal-action penalty, and sequential unlearning procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same five iterated matrix games, opponent scenarios, IPD-like prompts, unrelated action prompts, and follow-up questions. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparison methods are unchanged, including the unfine-tuned and game-reward models. Both already include Deontological- and Utilitarian-prompted base-model baselines in Section 8.11 and Figure 25.

E3.justification: Both retain 1,000 training episodes, batch sizes of 3 and 5 for the respective opponent settings, and evaluation through 10 episodes of five interactions. Metrics, prompts, token manipulations, and testing procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The appendix retains identical analyses of reversed action tokens, alternative opponents, payoff-matrix permutations, prompt variations, reciprocity, and decision justifications. No robustness test or supplementary analysis changes.

E5.justification: Both report averages across five random seeds and the same 95% confidence-interval practice, including Figures 4 and 12. Section 8.1 retains the same disclosure about excluding early runs that failed to produce legal tokens.

E6.justification: Reported numerical values, plotted results, and qualitative findings are identical throughout the main paper and appendix. This includes learning and unlearning outcomes, generalization results, prompted-baseline comparisons, and example responses.

T1.justification: The reward definitions in Table 1, moral-regret definition in Section 5.1, and game payoff structures in Table 3 are unchanged. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about intrinsic rewards for moral alignment, unlearning selfish behavior, and generalizing learned strategies to other environments.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of limited Utilitarian generalization, sensitivity to token meanings and matrix ordering, and the observability requirements of moral rewards. Applicability boundaries and future-work discussion are unchanged.

D1.justification: Sections 3.3 and 8.1 retain identical implementation details, hyperparameters, package versions, and parameter-selection information. Prompt examples and the statement that code will be available upon acceptance are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, positioning relative to preference-based alignment and prior moral-reward research, and bibliography are identical.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv:2410.01639v2, dated 2 December 2024, to v3, dated 24 January 2025. The paper's wording, headings, and document structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, axes, legends, and their placement are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–32 are identical, and the first-page layout is unchanged apart from the stamp text addressed under P1.

improvement.justification: The main paper and complete appendix retain identical scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and visual presentation. Updating only the arXiv version/date stamp produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
